result.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Advancing Harmful Content Understanding via Perception-Aware Adversarial Self-Play
result.summary: Despite significant advances in language understanding, Large Language Models (LLMs) can still miss meaning hidden in plain sight, failing to identify harmful intent in expressions readily understood by humans. Malicious users exploit this gap by strategically disguising harmful content to evade automated moderation, posing a serious threat to online platform safety. The vulnerability reflects a fundamental cognitive asymmetry between human readers, who integrate contextual, phonetic, and visual cues to decipher the intent behind deliberate obfuscation, and text-based LLMs, which rely primarily on token sequences and have limited exposure to evolving evasions. To bridge this asymmetry, we propose PASP (Perception-Aware Adversarial Self-Play), which combines multi-perceptual views with adversarial self-play to improve understanding of harmful intent as evasions evolve. Specifically, PASP constructs textual, phonetic, and visual views of each input, preserving its original context while exposing pronunciation and glyph cues obscured in token space. During adversarial self-play, an attacker uses defender feedback to generate intent-preserving evasions, while the defender is trained using an intent-invariance reward to understand harmful intent across changing surface forms. Extensive experiments show that PASP reduces adaptive attack success rates by up to 73.71% and 74.49% on ChineseHarm-Bench and EvoHarmBench, respectively, preserves model capabilities with minimal degradation, and effectively interprets real-world evasive expressions in e-commerce.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PASP，为每条输入构造文本、语音、视觉（字形）三种感知视图，并用攻防自博弈训练：攻击方借助防守方反馈生成保留意图的伪装表达，防守方以意图不变性奖励学习识别被伪装的有害意图，在中文有害内容基准上大幅降低自适应攻击成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 与主线无直接关系，但可核查的方法线索是：把 token 空间中丢失的字形/视觉线索显式放入表征视图，并用自博弈加意图不变性奖励迫使判断跨表面形式保持一致，这或可迁移为 latent 推理状态保留视觉细节、抵抗改写扰动的训练监督思路。
